paragraphs: Chapter 818
Episode 204. Declaration of War (5)
Satrine headed to the basement of the Tower of Tales where the magic stone was stored.
Meanwhile, at the flagship of the red fleet, Vilka Hon was evaluating Zipfel's fleet.
"As expected, except for the ship named Cojec, the rest are just average. They are even below the level of the ships that the Blue Plutonian race used to ride."
Vilka Hon said. Since there were no great warrior kings in the fleet that attacked the Tower of Tales, he, as a first-class warrior king, was in command.
"In my opinion too, Vilka brother, their firepower, mobility, defense, they can't compete with our fleet in any aspect."

"It's a shame, if I had been selected as the great warrior king, I could have led more ships and given them a significant blow before retreating. But now, the difference in numbers is too great, so there's nothing we can do."
Although the technology of the red race was overwhelmingly superior, they couldn't defeat 500 with 70. Since the purpose was reconnaissance anyway, Vilka was preparing to retreat slowly.
"I will open the dimensional gate. Other brothers have said that there are many monster-like humans in Zipfel too. They could move all of a sudden, so we can't let our guard down until the end."
Since Vilka's fleet did not have a great warrior king, it took much more time to open a dimensional gate.
"Red name!"
Zipfel's ships couldn't easily penetrate the protective shield of the red fleet. They couldn't surround the red fleet because of the lack of mobility.
Therefore, Vilka and his crew felt superior, but they were also feeling an odd sense of unease.

'But it's strange. Why haven't the so-called superhumans joined the front line so far? Did they spread all the superhumans to other first-class magic towers and plan to protect the Tower of Tales with just the fleet? Then it's even more unfortunate that our great warrior king brothers are missing.'

Vilka didn't know yet that Veradin and Satrine, and numerous spectral squad and ghost members were inside the tower. Since they were not participating in the battle, he had no other choice but to think that way.
The unease that the red race felt began to turn into a terrible sense of crisis about ten minutes later.
"The dimensional gate will open soon!"
"Gather all the fleets, prepare to retreat."
"The dimensional gate is fully opened! Uh, wa, wait. Brother Vilka! Something is strange!"
"What do you mean?"
"The di, dimensional gate is distorting...!"
At that, Vilka doubted his ears, and the next moment he had to doubt his eyes when he immediately checked the dimensional gate.
Crreeeaaak, Zzeeeeee...!
Some unknown force was distorting the dimensional gate that had opened behind the fleet. The dimensional gate only maintained a perfect circular shape for a brief moment.
"What's going on!"
"I don't know, there's no problem with the settings and the required power, what on earth...!"
None of the Red name race who attacked the Tower of Tales had ever experienced such a phenomenon.
'I've heard of brothers who have seen the Blue Plutonian race's warrior god blocking the dimensional gate, but this wasn't like that. Distorted to the point of being torn apart?'
The dimensional gate was already torn into several pieces, making the air confusing. The torn appearance seemed to be mocking them.
[Red name race, are you prepared to pay for daring to attack Zipfel?]
A voice came from the torn dimensional gate.
It was Veradin's voice. Vilka felt his throat dry up and reflexively checked the Tower of Tales.
'Wh, when did it change like that?'
The tower was now vertically split into two, unlike at first. There was a round and giant object that looked like an eye in the middle.
It was the magic stone.
Hiiiiii...
Soon the magic stone turned into a black face and made a strange breath. Unlike the Black Imperial Palace and the Evil Deity Palace, the magic stone had only one hollow eye hole.
Those from the Red name race who met the gaze of the one and only eye were frozen. Like animals facing their natural predators.
Vilka scratched his throat with his fingernails and barely managed to voice out. Even though a chunk of flesh fell from his neck, he couldn't feel the pain because of the fear.
"Raise the speed! We'll retreat from the battlefield by flying for now!"
If the red fleet retreats at full speed, Zipfel's fleet can't possibly follow. Therefore, Vilka judged that they should first get away from where the magic stone could be seen.

But even as he gave the order, he couldn't be sure. Even if the fleet doesn't know, that terrifying thing didn't seem like it would leave them alone. He hadn't experienced what kind of abilities the magic stone had, how dangerous it was, but he knew. That thing was not something that could be handled with their fleet.
The Red name race hurriedly supplied energy to the power source. They were desperate to get away from the magic stone right now, or they thought they would face death.

Or they were afraid that they might pay more than the cost of death. The fear that they might not only become immortal soldiers, but also become test subjects and experience horrific things was eroding their minds.
[You probably thought you could always run away using the dimensional gate. But this is the Tower of Tales. Without my permission, no one can realize their will.]
At the moment when the red fleet was trying to speed up, a man walked out from the torn dimension in front of the flagship. It was Veradin Zipfel, the head of the Zipfel family.
Heroti was holding a flame. The flame spread in an instant to create a massive wall of fire, and the red fleet couldn't get through it.
It was clear that the entire hull would melt. Veradin was floating in mid-air with an emotionless face. As he swung Heroti once, the flame concentrated and burned the flagship of the red fleet.
About twenty crew members turned to ashes, and nearly half of the hull disappeared, but the flagship did not crash due to Veradin's magic.
Veradin withdrew the flame after the front of the bridge was completely destroyed. The crew members who were sitting in front of Vilka all turned to ashes or met their death half melted.
He's not human.
Or, he's not mortal. Only those who have received the power of immortality from the sun can exert such authority.
Vilka thought so and managed to look at Veradin's face. He was striding through the sky and stepping into the bridge.
[What is your name.]
"Vilka... Hon. Red name race's, first-class warrior king."
[What is the purpose of your visit here?]
"Scouting..."
[What do you need to do next?]
"Return... and report... the situation."
Vilka was trembling as if in pain and drooling. Every time Veradin asked a question, his fear-filled eyes gradually turned blank.
[I'll ask again. What do you need to do next?]
"Return... No, to Zipfel... information about us. What, what are you doing to me, aaaargh!"
Snap!
Vilka's right arm twisted grotesquely all of a sudden. It was not what Veradin wanted.
[Ah, I see. Did I go too far.]
Veradin was currently manipulating Vilka's memories and will, and the history of 'Vilka Hon' using the magic stone.
But it was less precise than Veradin's expectations, causing an overload. Veradin furrowed his brows and sighed.
'It's twisted with resistance to the manipulation. If I hadn't lost my father and Sheenu, I would have succeeded easily in this.'
When Veradin released the 'manipulation' in progress, Vilka fell forward, gasping for air. He couldn't remember what he was talking about until just now, or why his right arm was twisted.
Also, there was serious damage to the memories and inner thoughts he had built up over time.
'Why am I here? What's this situation... were we in a battle? Who is this human, did I actually get beaten by a human. Why is this so, scary.'
Veradin immediately recognized Vilka's desperate state and sighed.
[What is your name?]
"Vilka... Hon..."
[Are you the first-class warrior king of the Red Name Race?]
Vilka slowly nodded his head.

'He remembers his name, affiliation, and rank. Fortunately, the damage isn't very severe. I almost ruined a valuable resource. Although he's not a grand warrior king, he was a commander anyway, so he should be able to provide the most information.'
As if testing,

Veradin applied manipulation to the soldier squatting next to Vilka. Then, before the soldier could even answer his name, he died with his neck twisted. On the other side, the second-class warrior king was able to endure a little more.
'It seems that ranks called warrior kings can somewhat withstand the pressure of manipulation. A certain level of resistance appears to be possessed by all members of the Red Name Race...'
In that case, the warrior kings would have to be carefully manipulated over time to extract information, and the rest could be interrogated.
Veradin concluded this and turned his body.

[Lock them all up in the basement of the tower. Separate the warrior kings. The ships probably have a device to prevent technological leakage. Self-destruction is the most likely, so keep them on standby in the Teia plains until the best engineers arrive.]
"Understood."
The fleet commanders responded from inside the ship. Veradin could hear all of their voices.
[And fleets 2 and 3, immediately withdraw and support the phantom commander as quickly as possible.]
As soon as he finished his command, Veradin staggered momentarily and spat out a mouthful of blood.
'Indeed, I pushed myself a little too much. I showed a pathetic state.'
Then he turned his body and looked at the rocky area far away from the tower of narrative. From the moment he opened the magic stone, Veradin was sure that there was a group watching him there.
He was also sure that Jin was in that group.
"... Owl commander. Veradin is looking at us right now."
"Given these conditions, this distance, even if it's Chiron commander, he wouldn't be able to spot my hiding. But the feeling is chilling, is it the power of the magic stone."

Unlike Owl, Jin wasn't too shocked by the fact that Veradin recognized them. The item called a magic stone still had unknown precise abilities and limitations. The same was true when the Red Name Race was suppressed as soon as the tower was opened.
He just found it bitter that his friend was becoming further away from being human.
"Huh, I'd like to go and hit him until he comes to his senses, but I think it's best to withdraw for today."
"Okay, get ready."
While Owl was preparing, Jin and Veradin did not take their eyes off each other.
